question: Pallavi bought a toy for ₹670, decorated it at a cost of ₹10 and sold the toy for ₹290. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) = 670 + 10 = 680.

Selling Price (SP) = 290.

Since SP [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Purchasing Price** = 670, **Overhead Expenses** = 10, **Selling Price (SP)** = 290.
Formulas: Total CP = Purchasing Price + Overhead Expenses | Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/919e03e712c7a508edf8390adf655a5ced20650e848e1d9ec65c401728c9743c.png] 
⇒ Total **Cost Price (CP)** = 670 + 10 = 680.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 290.
⇒ **Loss** = 680 − 290 = 390.
⇒ **Loss percentage** = (390 ÷ 680) × 100.
⇒ Loss% = (3900 ÷ 68)% = (975 ÷ 17)%.

**∴ The correct answer is (975)/(17)% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Price

The total cost price includes the original purchase price plus any **overhead expenses** like transportation, repairs, or decoration.

Loss Condition

A **loss** occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is less than the total Cost Price (CP). Loss% is always calculated on the **Cost Price**.</p
